item.text:
**5B.6 Research Note**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning **yes on intent/reform activity**, but **not yet on broad realized outcomes**. In 2024, Sisi’s government did invest in the foundations of productivity, especially education reform, public investment management, social/health infrastructure, and regulatory reform. But the best sources also say major capacity gaps remained, and access problems in education and health stayed serious.

**Evidence for yes**
- [World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts) | World Bank Group | 2024-03-18 | The World Bank says Egypt’s 2024 program backed private-sector growth and job creation, human capital outcomes through health and education, climate-smart resilience, and strengthened economic management. This is direct support for long-run productivity foundations. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report - Public Investment Management Assessment](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051) | IMF | 2024-04-02 | The IMF says Egypt had already taken steps to improve infrastructure access and public investment management through new legislation, new information systems, and staff-capacity efforts. It also notes ongoing health infrastructure roll-out and the Education 2.0 overhaul. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`

- [Egypt: Preparing Students for Life and the Workplace of Tomorrow](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/05/21/egypt-preparing-students-for-life-and-the-workplace-of-tomorrow) | World Bank | 2024-05-21 | The World Bank describes a live education reform program with new exams, teacher training, quality assurance, digital learning resources, and education technology. That is strong evidence of investment in human capital and technology for productivity. | `5B.6`

- [New World Bank US$700 million Support to Help Egypt Achieve More Sustainable, Diversified and Resilient Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/new-world-bank-us-700-million-support-to-help-egypt-achieve-more-sustainable-diversified-and-resilient-growth) | World Bank Group | 2024-06-24 | The new DPF supported stronger SOE governance, competition policy, payroll-tax assessment, lower electricity-distribution losses, water and sanitation sustainability, renewables, and a carbon-credit regulatory framework. That is direct evidence of investment in infrastructure and predictable regulation. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [IMF Executive Board Completes the First and Second Reviews of the EFF for Egypt](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/29/pr24101-egypt-imf-executive-board-completes-first-second-reviews-eff-approves-augmentation) | IMF | 2024-03-29 | The IMF says the stabilization plan centered on a flexible exchange rate, tighter policy, reducing public investment, and leveling the playing field so the private sector could drive growth. That supports the productivity foundation story, though it is still mainly macro-correction. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`

**Evidence against / limits**
- [Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report - Public Investment Management Assessment](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051) | IMF | 2024-04-02 | The same IMF report says PIM effectiveness is weaker than comparators in several institutions and recommends better appraisal, selection, maintenance, procurement, and portfolio management. That is a clear sign that administrative capacity remained incomplete. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`

- [Egypt: Preparing Students for Life and the Workplace of Tomorrow](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/05/21/egypt-preparing-students-for-life-and-the-workplace-of-tomorrow) | World Bank | 2024-05-21 | The World Bank also says Egypt still faces overcrowding, teacher shortages, low kindergarten enrollment, private-tutoring pressure, and a short school year. So the education system was being reformed, but the productivity base remained weak. | `5B.6`

- [Egypt: New law threatens to reduce access to healthcare for millions](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-new-law-threatens-to-reduce-access-to-healthcare-for-millions/) | Amnesty International | 2024-07-30 | Amnesty says Law 87 of 2024 privatized management of public health facilities without price regulation and was rushed through without adequate consultation. That cuts against a predictable, broadly accessible health system. | `5B.6`

- [Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | HRW says bureaucratic residency requirements, fees, and discrimination kept tens of thousands of refugee children out of school. This is not the whole education system, but it shows access remained uneven and exclusionary. | `5B.6`

**Synthesis**
- Strongest positive evidence: education reform, digital learning, public-investment-management reform, SOE/utility/regulatory reforms, and ongoing health-infrastructure rollout.
- Strongest negative evidence: weak implementation capacity, persistent school overcrowding and teacher shortages, and a rushed health-law change that risks reducing access.
- Best reading for 2024: Sisi **did invest** in productivity foundations, but the record looks more like **unfinished reform under stress** than a fully effective transformation of schools, hospitals, infrastructure governance, or regulatory predictability.

**Search gap**
- I found good evidence on reform design and partial rollout, but not strong 2024 proof of broad nationwide outcome gains in learning, health outcomes, or service reliability. The sources mostly show intent, financing, and institutional steps, not durable results.
